boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Corydon record (July 9, 1863) in Morgan's Raid in Kentucky, Indiana, and Ohio [July 1863]. The Ohio River crossing at Brandenburg and Mauckport on July 8 is context, not part of the engagement interval. The raid's start strength, detachments, captures and campaign effects span July 2–26 and several engagements; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen and live fields give 2,200 (US 400; CS 1,800). NPS says Morgan entered Kentucky on July 2 with about 2,450 hand-picked cavalrymen and that elements of his force met about 400 Home Guards near Corydon. Duke gives 2,460 effective men at the Cumberland crossing, exclusive of four guns; at Corydon he describes Colonel [R. C.] Morgan's advance guard and one regiment of the second brigade. Burnside wrote on July 22 that Morgan's force when he entered Indiana did not vary far from 3,000 men.
claims.rationale: Start-of-raid, Indiana-entry and engaged-element figures differ in scope; Duke's 2,460 and Burnside's 3,000 conflict. None is adopted as matched opening strength.

claims.value: NPS says Morgan rode to disrupt the communications of the Army of the Cumberland and crossed the Ohio despite orders to remain in Kentucky. Duke, who says he was not present at the interview, relays Morgan's account that Bragg ordered him to confine himself to Kentucky and that Morgan intended nevertheless to cross the Ohio, arguing that a raid into Indiana and Ohio would draw the troops in Kentucky after him.
claims.rationale: Stated aims from a summary and an interested, secondhand history; orders not separately inspected.

The frozen commanders are Lewis Jordan, Brevet Colonel, and John Hunt Morgan, Brigadier General; the live heading gives Colonel Lewis Jordan. No inspected passage describes Jordan's command.
claims.rationale: Command roles from an interested history; the frozen commanders do not receive automatic sole credit, and the live rank is not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 401 (US 360; CS 41); the live field reads 411 (US 360; CS 51). Duke says the militia killed and wounded several men, including Lieutenant Thorpe. Burnside's compiled return of Union casualties for the raid, July 2–26, names volunteer, regular and garrison commands but no Indiana militia unit; its OCR total row reads 1, 18, 3, 44, 8 and 74, the last equalling the sum of the others (a computation here).
claims.rationale: Frozen and live Confederate counts differ. The raid-wide return does not account for the Corydon militia and is not assigned to this record; no canonical reconciliation.

open_questions: Indiana Legion and Jordan's own reports, and the scope of the frozen 360 Union casualties (captured militia versus killed and wounded), remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Duke's History of Morgan's Cavalry (1867) is an interested Confederate participant history: Duke commanded a brigade on the raid by his own account and was captured at Buffington, so his account of later days is not eyewitness. The Burnside, Hobson and Shackelford reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXIII, Part 1, are interested Union accounts. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
